examples.text: Повара не должны быть на арене!
examples.trans: Cooks should not be in an arena!
Citizen Anikeev, you are under arrest.
We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: at home, a party, or a restaurant

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'cooking, food preparation' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Гости любят смотреть на процесс готовки.
examples.trans: Guests love watching the cooking process.
We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

зато.gloss: but on the other hand, to make up for it

meanings.en: but on the other hand, at least

examples.text: Четыре по алгебре, зато по физкультуре пятёрка.
examples.trans: A four in algebra, but a five in gym.
The flat is small, but at least it's in the centre.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Сейчас зато аппетит нагуляем.
examples.trans: No big deal. At least we'll walk up an appetite now.
Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: an insult: someone who isn't serious

examples.trans: A clown works at the circus.
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: на его место = in his place

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fashionable, trendy, stylish').

examples.trans: This is a trendy open kitchen format.

examples.text: Это слово «модный» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'fashionable' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: остаётся у нас = stays with us

examples.trans: And the advance stays with us.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крытый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('open, unclosed').

examples.trans: This is a trendy open kitchen format.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.
Can I go and have a look?

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

meanings.note: по порядку = in order; всё в порядке = everything is fine

examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order.

examples.text: Теперь давай всё по порядку. Скажи мне, сколько ты им должна?
examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order. Tell me, how much do you owe them?

meanings.note: person visiting a person, place, or institution

examples.trans: A visitor was sitting in the reception room.

examples.text: Это журнал посетителей мэрии из полицейских вещдоков.
examples.trans: This is the mayor's visitor log from police evidence.

examples.text: Зато в ресторане станет больше посетителей.
examples.trans: On the other hand, there will be more patrons in the restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'влечение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attraction, engagement' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Она нужна для привлечения новых гостей.
examples.trans: It is needed to attract new guests.

examples.text: Это слово «привлечение» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'attraction' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'зрачный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('transparent, clear').

examples.trans: Why do we need this transparent wall?

examples.text: Мне сказали, что выборы должны пройти честно. Честно и прозрачно!
examples.trans: They told me that the election must be conducted honestly. Honestly and transparently!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'цесс'). Common masculine noun meaning 'process, trial' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну и процесс остановился. Да арестовывать его надо, товарищ генерал!
examples.trans: And so the process stalled. We just need to arrest him, Comrade General!

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'поряжение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'order, instruction, directive' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Victoria Sergeyevna's order, chef.

examples.text: Это слово «распоряжение» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'order' is often heard in conversation.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вященный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sacred, holy').

examples.trans: The kitchen must remain a sacred place.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'теклянный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('glass, glassy').

examples.text: Это что ещё за стеклянный аквариум?
examples.trans: What kind of glass aquarium is this?

examples.text: Это слово «стеклянный» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'glass' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: of a room, building or fortress

examples.trans: The picture is on the wall.

examples.text: Не надо врать. Стену монастыря сносят!
examples.trans: Don't lie. They're pulling down the monastery wall!

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'format, layout' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a trendy open kitchen format.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: movement by foot or figurative action

examples.text: Надо следить за каждым шагом соперника.
examples.trans: We must monitor every step of the rival.

examples.text: Надо следить за каждым шагом кандидата.
examples.trans: We must monitor every step of the candidate.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
